messages.author: 0c69c6d399345fab
messages.subject: Piecewise Regression with multiple predictors
parts:
Hi All,

I'm working on a project where I'm interested in estimating community index thresholds (e.g., functional diversity) for multiple predictors. With that in mind, I'm implementing a sort of piecewise regression model in JAGS. Ideally, I'd like to be able to include other predictors in the model but they would only be represented as standard betas in the model (i.e., not estimating threshold parameters for them). If I only include the predictor for which I wish to estimate the threshold response (in the code below "TWY"), the model runs fine in JAGS. However, if I include the other predictors as standard betas in the model, the following error is produced " Dimension mismatch, taking subset of stream1". I know this has to do with the inclusion of the other predictors, I just cannot seem to identify the  root cause of the error. Also, one more question along that same line: would it be possible to include multiple predictors for which I wish to estimate multiple threshold responses in the same model? This seems to be possible in R, but I cannot find any BUGS code to fit a similar model in JAGS. 

As always, any help provided is more than appreciated!

Thanks,

Josh

Code below, data attached

#Upload Data
data<-read.csv("LS_Summer_dat.csv", header = T)

y<- (data[,7])/100
n<-nrow(data)
site<- nrow(data)

#Predictors
Stream1<- data[8]
Stream2<- data[9]
Land1<- data[10]
Land2<- data[11]
TWY<- standardize(data[,12])

#data for covariate model
jags.data<-list(y=y,n.sites=n,M=site, Stream1=Stream1, Stream2=Stream2,
                Land1=Land1, Land2=Land2, TWY=TWY)

########################
########################  
require(jagsUI)
sink("model1.txt")
cat("
 model{
 #priors
   
 phi~ dgamma(0.1,0.1)
 beta ~ dunif(-3,3)
 beta1 ~ dunif(-3,3)
 beta2 ~ dunif(-3,3)
 beta3 ~ dunif(-3,3)
 beta4 ~ dunif(-2,2)
 x.change ~ dunif(-2,2)

 #Random Intercepts
 mu_int~dnorm(0, 0.001) # Mean hyperparameter for random intercepts
 sd_int~dunif(0, 1) # SD hyperparameter for random intercepts
 tau_int <- 1/(sd_int*sd_int)
 
 
 for (i in 1:M) {
    alpha0[i]~ dnorm(mu_int, tau_int)
 }
 
 #likelihood
 for(i in 1:n.sites) {
  y[i] ~ dbeta(a[i], b[i])
  a[i] <- mu[i] * phi
  b[i]  <- (1-mu[i]) * phi
  logit(mu[i])<-alpha0[i] + beta*Stream1[i] + beta1*Stream2[i]
   + beta2*Land1[i] + beta3*Land2[i] +
  beta4*(TWY[i]-x.change)*step(TWY[i] - x.change)
 }
 }
  ",fill=TRUE)
sink()

##Parameters to Estimate
params<-c("mu_int","beta", "beta1","beta2", "beta3", "beta4","x.change")

model1 <- jagsUI(data=jags.data, parameters.to.save=params, 
                 model.file="model1.txt",n.thin =10,n.chains = 3, 
                 n.burnin = 10000, n.iter =500000,parallel=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Piecewise Regression with multiple predictors
parts:
Hi all,

I came across this post which greatly piqued my interest as I'm actually attempting to do something similar with my research, but with a multi-species occupancy model, and I'm trying to figure out how to best specify this in JAGS.

For my own research I am interested in examining whether there is a threshold between percent forest cover and mammal species richness in my study area, across sites with varying levels of forest cover, specifically to see if there is a threshold point where species richness steeply declines once the level of forest cover in a given site hits below a particular point. I'll attach my code below where I attempt to specify where/how I might specify the threshold point in the likelihood, but I'm not sure if this is correct, and where else I might need to specify the threshold throughout the model as it's a multi-species model.

Also, since richness is a derived quantity from these models, I'm curious as to whether it makes sense to specify the threshold within the multi-species occupancy model, or doing a secondary analysis in a piecewise/break point regression model (by using the segmented package for example) using the richness outputs across sites and the % forest cover covariates to look for a forest cover threshold would be a better/more straight forward option to examine this?

Any input on this would be greatly appreciated, thank you!

Best,,

Jordan
